candidates.core_provocation: In a future subway station, people can borrow other citizens’ memories for a few minutes. A grieving woman discovers that a stranger has checked out her only memory of her dead daughter—and the memory will be changed forever when it is returned, so she must find the stranger before the train leaves.
candidates.why_interesting: It turns grief into a tense public chase while asking whether anyone can truly own a memory.

candidates.core_provocation: In a future public square, people can pay to erase painful memories, and the erased memories are stored until they are destroyed. A man waiting to delete the memory of his wife’s death recognizes himself in one of the anonymous memories and realizes he may have forgotten the reason she died.
candidates.why_interesting: The suspense comes from deciding whether discovering the truth is worth recovering unbearable pain.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first idea has the clearest immediate action, a small cast, and a natural time limit. The stranger’s loss also complicates the protagonist’s goal, creating both emotional tension and a surprising question about who has the right to reclaim a memory.
